items.title: Burnham to tell MPs he wants to ‘unlock positivity’ in first Commons statement as PM – UK politics live
items.summary: After cabinet meeting this morning, prime minister will talk about plans to bring more essential services back into public control to boost growth My colleague Richard Partington, the Guardian’s senior economics correspondent, grew up, like Andy Burnham, in the Warrington suburb of Culcheth. He has been home to find out what people there are saying about the new PM. Yesterday, Kemi Badenoch announced a reshuffle, replacing Mel Stride with Andrew Griffith as shadow chancellor and Priti Patel with Tom Tugendhat…

items.title: Can Ancient Ruins Be Protected From Wildfires? Greece Is Trying.
items.summary: As blazes surge across Europe, the country is making a trade-off to protect its heritage by fireproofing sites at the risk of spoiling the surrounding landscape.

items.title: UK long-term borrowing costs hit 28-year high
items.summary: Yield on 30-year government bonds jumps to 5.88%, the highest since 1998, in bond rout triggered by global factors Business live – latest updates The UK government’s long-term borrowing costs jumped to their highest level since early 1998 on Tuesday as a global bond sell-off gathered pace. The yield – in effect the interest rate – on 30-year UK government bonds, known as gilts, hit 5.89% as traders fretted about a fresh increase in oil prices driving up inflation. Continue…

items.title: Punishment and Silence: China Pulls Out the Disaster Playbook in Tibet
items.summary: While journalists can report freely on grief and anger in Nepal, China’s official media have presented a sanitized disaster aftermath in Tibet.

items.title: Man, 23, appears in court charged with murder after Teesside house fire
items.summary: Seven-year-old girl and aunt, 34, died and four others were injured in blaze near Middlesbrough last week A 23-year-old man has appeared in court charged with murdering a seven-year-old girl and her aunt who died in a house fire. Natalie McDonald, 34, and Valentina Foster died and four other people were injured in the blaze in Grangetown, near Middlesbrough, in the early hours of 26 August. Continue reading...

items.summary: The U.S.S. Abraham Lincoln became an emblem of the strains of the war on the U.S. military. Now its crew will have some rest.

items.title: London Stock Exchange to lose three more firms after takeover offers
items.summary: Latest purchases take value of deals to leave capital’s stock market this year past $100bn Three more London-listed companies are set to be taken over as the value of deals removing firms from the capital’s under-pressure stock market so far this year passes $100bn (£74bn). On Tuesday, Bodycote, the FTSE 250 industrials group that has been listed on the London Stock Exchange since 1972, agreed a £1.84bn takeover by the US private equity group Veritas. items.title: How the Supreme Court Locks Away Its Own History
items.summary: Supreme Court justices could keep the court’s internal working papers hidden for decades. Our investigative reporter Jodi Kantor explains why those records matter — and what sealing them away means for our understanding of key decisions by the nation’s highest court.

items.title: A Factory in Rural Ireland Is at the Center of a Dispute Over Russia
